Two issues:

1. `_call`'s `body=object()` sentinel: when body not given, `data` stays None — wait the error "Object of type object is not JSON serializable" — hmm, in `_call`, `if body is not object()` — each call `object()` default is evaluated once at def time... Actually default argument `body=object()` creates one sentinel instance. Inside I compare `body is not object()` — a NEW object each call! So sentinel never matches. Fix: define module-level sentinel `_UNSET = object()` and compare with it.

2. CLI subparser: parent args must come before subcommand `verify`. `audit verify --tenant-id ...` fails because argparse subparsers don't share parent options after the subcommand. The README/requirement wants `audit verify` as a subcommand; users naturally write `audit verify --tenant-id t --operator alice`. To support that, give the verify subparser its own `--tenant-id` and `--operator` arguments (like policy subcommands do: `policy --operator admin show --tenant-id t` — there operator is on parent, tenant on child).

Simplest: add `--tenant-id` (required) and `--operator` (required) to the verify subparser itself. Then both `audit --tenant-id t --operator alice verify` and `audit verify --tenant-id t --operator alice`? If args exist on both parent and child with same dest, argparse handles them separately; the child's parsed namespace defaults could override parent values? With nested subparsers, argparse merges into one namespace: parent sets tenant_id, then subparser default (None) overwrites unless `default=argparse.SUPPRESS` on child. Use `default=argparse.SUPPRESS` on child args so they don't clobber parent-set values. That supports both orders. Update tests to put args after verify (natural form). Also flat audit query unaffected.

raw_content:
argparse requires parent's required args even when a subparser is used, because parent parsing sees missing required arguments before handing to subparser. The policy command avoids this by putting `--operator` on the parent `policy` parser (still required!) and tenant on children — so `policy --operator admin show --tenant-id t` order. With required parent args, they must appear before the subcommand.

Options:
1. Make parent `--tenant-id/--operator` not required on audit parser and instead validate manually (like provider does). But flat audit query relies on required; can validate in dispatch. This gives flexible ordering both ways.
2. Keep required and document/use order `audit --tenant-id t --operator alice verify`.

The natural UX and README example is `audit verify --tenant-id t --operator alice`. Go with option 1: create audit parser without tenant_parser helper — add optional args with defaults, and in dispatch for both flat query and verify, validate presence/non-empty (existing dispatch already checks `if not args.tenant_id`; operator is checked globally: `if not getattr(args, "operator", None)` → exit 2). Missing operator → currently global check yields "field operator must be a non-empty string" exit 2. Fine.

But flat `audit --key-id x` with no tenant → currently argparse error exit 2; after change, our code returns the same 400-style body exit 2 ("field tenant_id must be a non-empty string"). Acceptable and consistent.

Subparser args: use plain `--tenant-id`/`--operator` with default SUPPRESS so values after `verify` fill namespace and parent's optional ones before also work.

Implement: change `p_audit = tenant_parser("audit", ...)` to manual:

```python
p_audit = sub.add_parser("audit", help="list a tenant's audit events")
p_audit.add_argument("--tenant-id", default=None)
p_audit.add_argument("--operator", default=None, help="...")
```

Child verify args also default SUPPRESS so they don't clobber (when given on parent, child parser action with SUPPRESS won't overwrite). Actually careful: argparse subparsers parse into the same namespace and the child action default of SUPPRESS means if child arg not provided, nothing happens. If parent provided, value remains. If child provided, set. 

One wrinkle: `--operator` after verify while parent's global dispatch uses args.operator — same namespace, works.

The natural UX and README example is `audit verify --tenant-id t --operator alice`. Go with option 1: create audit parser without tenant_parser helper — add optional args with defaults, and in dispatch for both flat query and verify, validate presence/non-empty (existing dispatch already checks `if not args.tenant_id`; operator is checked globally: `if not getattr(args, "operator", None)` → exit 2). Missing operator → currently global check yields "field operator must be a non-empty string" exit 2. Fine.

But flat `audit --key-id x` with no tenant → currently argparse error exit 2; after change, our code returns the same 400-style body exit 2 ("field tenant_id must be a non-empty string"). Acceptable and consistent.

Subparser args: use plain `--tenant-id`/`--operator` with default SUPPRESS so values after `verify` fill namespace and parent's optional ones before also work.

Implement: change `p_audit = tenant_parser("audit", ...)` to manual:

p_audit.add_argument("--tenant-id", default=None)
p_audit.add_argument("--operator", default=None, help="...")

Child verify args also default SUPPRESS so they don't clobber (when given on parent, child parser action with SUPPRESS won't overwrite). Actually careful: argparse subparsers parse into the same namespace and the child action default of SUPPRESS means if child arg not provided, nothing happens. If parent provided, value remains. If child provided, set.
